utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-13a-I, the Prosecutor v Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Let me first verify that the equipment is operative. Can everyone who is using the earphones hear me in a language that they understand? Under our Rules the Tribunal records its proceedings and they are available to the public. I have issued an Order to that effect this morning. This is an initial appearance pursuant to Rule 62 of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. May I have the appearances, please, for the court? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours please, my name is Grant Niemann. I will be appearing for the Prosecution in this matter. My co-counsel, who is not here today, will be Mr Clint Williamson. At the Bar table I am assisted by Miss Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Niemann. May I have the appearances for the defence, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, my name is Toma Fila. I am attorney from Belgrade and defence counsel for the accused, Slavko Dokmanovic. My assistant and legal counsel is Mrs Jelena Lopicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Fila, you have been appointed by the Tribunal to represent the accused; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is the defence ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Fila, have you and Mr Dokmanovic received a copy of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, we have and we have understood both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Have you read to Mr Dokmanovic the indictment, or has it been read to him in a language that he understands?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It has been read to him, and he understands, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Have you had sufficient time to confer with Mr Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I did. I had sufficient time. We have consulted and we are ready for this initial appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you believe that Mr Dokmanovic understands the nature of the charges contained in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I believe he understands. I have given him a copy of the statute. He has read it through and he understands what he is charged with and he is quite ready to make a statement in that connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Dokmanovic, would you please rise? For the record, would you state your full name?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on 14th December 1949.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Have you received a copy of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Has it been read to you or have you read it in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have read it and it has been read to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Fila has been appointed as your counsel to represent -- pardon me. Mr Fila? I was just making reference to you. Mr Fila has been appointed as your counsel to represent you in this matter. Are you satisfied with that appointment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you believe that Mr Fila will represent you effectively before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you understand the nature of the charges contained in the indictment, Mr Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: And are you ready to enter a plea with respect to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Now, will the indictment be read out in its entirety, Mr Fila, or will Mr Dokmanovic waive the reading of the indictment in its entirety at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no need to read the indictment for me or for Mr Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Dokmanovic, how do you plead to Count 1 in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How do you plead to Count 2 of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How do you plead to Count 3 of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How do you plead to Count 4 of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How do you plead to Count 5 of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How do you plead to Count 6 of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Fine. Mr Dokmanovic, you will be remanded to the custody of the Detention Unit of the Tribunal until further order of the Court. You may be seated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Fila, have you received a copy of the material that accompanied the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Niemann, when will you provide counsel and the Defence with a copy of the material that accompanied the indictment when it was confirmed pursuant to Rule 66A of the Rules of Procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are at the moment just going through the material to ensure that there is no position with respect to witnesses in terms of protective measures, and we would hope to have fully satisfied that requirement within a period of 30 days, and during that period, if it is convenient to the court and satisfactory to the court, we would make available all of the material that was provided in support of the indictment, and together with what other material that we consider we will use at trial, which is in a position to be discovered at this stage, if that is satisfactory to the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Fila, under Rule 73 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence you are entitled to file preliminary motions and you are given a period of 60 days to file those motions. Do you anticipate that you will be filing any preliminary motions at this time, and, if so, when do you expect that they will be filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (Not translated).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have already prepared that motion, but according to the Rules we first have to have the preliminary appearance, and therefore my motion will be submitted to you by Monday. In the meantime I can review it once again. As for the disclosure of evidence under Rule 66, I think that 30 days is sufficient for other evidence, but I don't see why I need to wait 30 days for what was given to the Judge for the confirmation of the indictment. I feel I could have received that straightaway. As for the other material, 30 days is acceptable. Have I made myself clear, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, you've made yourself clear. Mr Niemann, why do you need 30 days? The Rule says as soon as practicable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Some of the material we can make available almost immediately but there are just other pieces of supporting material that we -- it is just a matter of caution -- are anxious to check to make sure. This may involve checking with the witnesses themselves, to make sure that protective measures aren't required. In our submission, because of the fact that witness protection issues are of very great concern to the Prosecution and indeed to the Tribunal, we need to be particularly careful and cautious with respect to material, having regard to experience we have had in the past. For that reason it takes longer than -- and it's not just a matter of bundling up the material and handing it over. That, of course, can be done as a mechanical measure. Then in doing so we haven't made adequate preparation for witness protection, should that be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I obviously have not seen the material that accompanied the indictment, but typically there is a brief that accompanies the indictment as well as statements, but it is not just statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you cannot provide immediately to Mr Fila all of the material that was submitted in support of the indictment when it was confirmed, except for the statements? That should be done today, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We can do that, your Honour. I am not sure it can be done today but we can certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not sure we can do it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, because there is quite a bit of copying involved in doing that and there is video films and so forth. I think it would take longer than today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How long will it take?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I could probably have it ready by Monday, if your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: By Monday, Mr Fila. Now with respect to the statements, is it not possible for you to redact those statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is, but it may not be necessary if protective measures are not required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It may, in fact, be quicker to hand over statements which we feel are not going to create a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: From the Defence's point of view it might be better for you to give the Defence the statements, redacting all of the names, and then at the same time proceed to contact these witnesses to determine whether they wish protective measures, and then you would file a motion and the trial chamber would then act on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Certainly we can do that in respect of witnesses that we are concerned about. There is no point in redacting where -- some of the witnesses will probably not create a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Then for those witnesses can you provide the statements to the Defence by Monday, for those for whom there is no problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: So then you will provide all of the material that accompanied the indictment, when it was confirmed, except for statements of witnesses for whom you believe there is a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, for whom we believe we need to enquire to see whether there is a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now for those for whom you need to enquire to see whether there is a problem, why can't those statements be redacted, that's the name of the witness giving the statement as well as any references in the body of the statements to witnesses? The reason is that -- well, there are a number of reasons, but the major reason is that the Defence -- the period of time allowed to the Defence for the filing of preliminary motion is 60 days. If they do not receive the material until 30 days, that has cut into their time. What I'm going to suggest is that the time period for the filing of preliminary motions begin to run from the date that you receive all of the material, Mr Fila, but I'm attempting to expedite, if at all possible, the Prosecution's providing the Defence with the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I certainly have no objection to the proposal that your Honour suggests for extending the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. So we will extend the time that the Defence has under Rule 73 to file preliminary motions until the time when you receive all of the material, and then that 60 days would begin to run. However, with respect to the material that you have that accompanied the indictment, except for witnesses for whom you believe there may be a problem regarding protective measures, that should be provided to Mr Fila by Monday. For the others, if you believe that there are problems or at least there may be a request for protective measures, I still don't understand why you can't provide that and redact the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Because it is not as easy as just redacting names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is often material in the body of the statement which would identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That would tend to identify. I have seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Unless we have adequate time to go through these and in some instances to actually consult the witnesses, we are not exactly sure what matters in the body of the statement may well go to identification. It is not a simple process of simply taking a black pen and rubbing out a pen. It is more than that. It is a much more complex process than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I don't want to be difficult, but perhaps that enquiry should be made when the statements are taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They are, your Honour but circumstances change. We don't take statements generally unless witnesses are willing to testify but circumstances happen. Things have been happening on a continual basis in relation to other trials that have been before this tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Exactly. Some of the things that have been happening are delays in providing the Defence with material and I want to avoid that in this instance. I want to start this -- I want to start the proceeding on a good foot, if you understand what I mean on a good foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I want to as much as possible encourage the Prosecution not to delay in providing the Defence with the material. I understand the concerns that you have but you have to understand the concerns that the Defence has. Then if the material is not provided promptly, then we encounter problems in terms of setting the trial, and that has occurred. So I want to try to avoid this. I am not suggesting that you are delaying intentionally. I am just suggesting a different approach in perhaps understanding the concerns of the Defence. Fine. If you understand then where we are, you will receive all of the material that accompanied the indictment by Monday, Mr Fila, except for statements which the Prosecution believes may come from or come from witnesses who may request protective measures. As for those statements, they will be provided to you no later than 30 days from today, and the period of time that you have under Rule 73 to file your preliminary motions will run from the date that you receive all of the material. Is that acceptable, Mr Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is a very specific problem that we are dealing with. The territory we are talking about, as learned counsel knows, Croatian authority is being established in the full sense of the word. I already need a visa to enter that area and I cannot enter it for a number of reasons, including my personal safety, so that people working in Vukovar now of Serbian nationality and who are already affected by the fact that only their names have been published and the method of arrest of Mr Dokmanovic, and we have communicated a great deal, Mr Niemann and I, so that I'm not insisting on knowing the names of any one of the witnesses that Mr Niemann will be proposing, not because their safety may be threatened by me or any one of my associates, but for me to know what they are saying and to be able to take advantage of the fact that there are still people in Vukovar who can provide me with certain documents. That is why I'm insisting on promptness. Mr Niemann knows why I am insisting on expediency. I'm ready to wait for more than 30 days to know the name of somebody who made a certain statement, but I beg to receive those statements as soon as possible, because every day is invaluable. I'm going to Belgrade tomorrow morning to try and obtain material which I assume Mr Niemann will be referring to accompanying the indictment, and that is why I appeal to you, and I insist on receiving the statements as soon as possible. It is the most -- the most important thing is not who made the statement but what will be used from that statement in support of the indictment. The important thing is that I know what they say, so that I can provide the Defence. I can prepare the Defence and the counter arguments. Thank you for your understanding, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Niemann, I gather you may face the same problems with respect to the territory and access to witnesses, etc; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not necessarily, your Honour, not in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Mr Niemann, I think you get the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Very good. Do as best you can, but no later than 30 days for everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to proceed to trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to proceed to trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, quite prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Subject to, I'm sure, the receipt of the material and subject to the filing of preliminary motions and the resolution of those motions by the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If I receive the material within 30 days, I will complete my part within the following 30 days, while my assistants can go there. When they are prevented from going there, then the trial will proceed in an improper way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps, your Honour, because of the unique situation that exists in this particular area and particularly because of the involvement of the United Nations we will endeavour to make enquiries to see whether or not we can more easily facilitate Mr Fila's access to this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Niemann. So, Mr Fila, then you would file, you expect, your preliminary motions, assuming -- I am sure Mr Niemann will meet the deadline of 30 days from today -- by about September 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, your Honour. You will receive my first motion on Monday. That is the one I do not need any material for. It has to do with the arrest, the method of arrest and the guarantees, if they are of any value to the Prosecution. The other motions deal with other problems, and I will be able to prepare my preliminary motions by 8th September. What I am trying to say is we are quite prepared for the beginning of trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Then, of course, after you file your preliminary motions, if you file them by September 8th, the Prosecution is typically afforded 14 days to respond. I don't know that it's appropriate at this time to set a date for trial, because it really would be an artificial date. It would not be a real date. I consider it might be more appropriate to set a status conference that would be after that 14-day period that the Prosecution has to respond to preliminary motions to ascertain where the parties are and then set a trial date after we have had that status conference. May I set a status conference for Monday, September 29th at 10.00 am? Now, I am concerned, though, that that is some distance away, and if the parties have any difficulties in terms of discovery, then, Mr Fila and Mr Niemann, you should contact the Trial Chamber, because we are always available and willing to resolve any difficulties, if we can resolve those difficulties, that you may have in the obtaining of evidence, that is at least the material that accompanied the indictment. That's our first concern. If there are any delays or if there are any other problems that occur, then, Mr Niemann or Mr Fila, you should contact the Tribunal by contacting the Registry, indicating that there is a problem and that you need to meet with the judges. If that is so, we will be available to meet with you. Is there anything else that we should consider at this time, Mr Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not from the point of view of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, as far as Defence counsel is concerned. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Then the Trial Chamber is adjourned. (10.30 am)
